thread.title_full: Marc Rardin agrees to four-year contract extension with WKU Baseball

author: k. n. lange
title: Marc Rardin agrees to four-year contract extension with WKU Baseball
text:
WKU Baseball Head Coach Marc Rardin has agreed to a four-year contract extension that will keep him at the helm through the 2030 season, Director of Athletics Todd Stewart announced on June 10 in Bowling Green, Kentucky.
Rardin has compiled a 145-89 record over his four seasons as head coach, achieving a .620 winning percentage—the best in WKU Baseball’s 107-year history. He led the Hilltoppers to their first Conference USA Tournament Championship in 2025, which secured an automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament and marked WKU’s first appearance since 2009.
During Rardin’s tenure, the Hilltoppers have posted the second-best winning percentage among Division I programs in Kentucky. The team has recorded at least 30 wins each season for four consecutive years. The total of 145 wins is also the second most by any WKU team over a four-year period.
Seven players from Rardin’s teams have signed with professional organizations during his time as head coach. Six remain active in their respective organizations, including Ryan Wideman, who was named Conference USA Player of the Year and earned All-American honors as an outfielder in 2025.
“Marc Rardin’s contract extension is much deserved, and we are thrilled he continues to lead our baseball program,” said Director of Athletics Todd Stewart. “He has produced one of the best four-year stretches in our program’s more than 100-year history after inheriting a program coming off an 18-36 season and 12th place finish in Conference USA. Under his leadership, we have recruited talented players with a winning mindset who play an exciting style of baseball while renewing confidence in our fan base. His phenomenal leadership and dedication have completely turned our program around.”
“Over four years ago, Todd Stewart trusted me to be the right guy to start making WKU Baseball relevant again,” said head coach Marc Rardin. “With our hard-working coaching staff, we have transformed every aspect of the program. While the work isn’t done and challenges are still in front of us, my family and I are thrilled that Todd and the WKU administration continue to believe in what we’re doing by giving us an extension to stay on The Hill.”
